title: Check: kubectl fundamentals
description: Five questions on the verbs, output formats and the shortcuts that save time.

questions.prompt: Write the command that lists Pods in every namespace.
questions.explanation: Graded with fuzzy matching: `-A` and `--all-namespaces` score the same, as do `po` and `pods`.

questions.prompt: What does `kubectl describe` give you that `kubectl get` does not?

options.text: Events and a human-readable summary of related state
A list of every object of that type

questions.explanation: `describe` assembles the object plus its events and related objects. For the raw stored form you want `get -o yaml`.

questions.prompt: Write the command that prints the YAML for a Deployment named web using image nginx, without creating anything.
questions.explanation: Generating a manifest and editing it is far faster under exam pressure than writing YAML from memory.

questions.prompt: You cannot remember which field sets a Pod's restart policy. Which command tells you without leaving the terminal?
questions.explanation: `kubectl explain` walks the schema field by field. It is the fastest documentation you have during the exam.

questions.prompt: Which of these actually save time in a two-hour exam? Choose all that apply.

options.text: `--dry-run=client -o yaml` to generate a starting manifest

questions.explanation: Everything that removes keystrokes helps. Writing YAML from memory is the one habit that reliably costs you time.
